title: Verdier hom chain composition
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified six operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Finite inputs used for compact support carry compatible etale-origin witnesses; integral inputs are derived complete with compatible witnessed finite reductions, rational operations are raw localization, and algebraically closed coefficients are represented at a common finite coefficient field. All operations below are restricted to their stated constructible domains; tensor factors and comparisons have their stated finite-Tor hypotheses. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type maps of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Assume $f,g,gf$ and the structure morphisms $a_X,a_Y,a_Z$ are exceptionally admissible as in [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. Set $F_f=Rf_!$, $P_f=Lf^*$, $H_X=R\mathcal Hom_X$, $\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, and $D_X=H_X(-,\omega_X)$, and similarly on $Y,Z$. For $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the canonical tensor-Hom exchange of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction] is represented, on finite-Tor constructible tests $T$, by the natural chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T,H_Y(F_fM,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_fM\otimes T,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_f(M\otimes P_fT),N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M\otimes P_fT,f^!N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rf_*H_X(M,f^!N)).$$
The middle bijection is induced by the inverse of the projection isomorphism $\operatorname{PF}_f$ of [fix-prop-projection-formula]. All representing objects and tests lie in the common constructible finite-Tor categories; thus the identity of a representing object is an allowed test. Specialization to $N=\omega_Y$ and the conjugate identification $f^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$ gives exactly the Verdier comparison of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange], $\varepsilon_{f,M}:D_YF_fM\cong Rf_*D_XM$. For $gf$, the Hom chain agrees on every input arrow with the successive chains for $g$ and $f$, after substituting the projection associativity pentagon, the pasted exceptional counit $\epsilon_g(F_g\epsilon_fG_g)$ and the canonical pullback/direct-image compositors. Consequently
$$\varepsilon_{gf,M}=Rg_*(\varepsilon_{f,M})\circ\varepsilon_{g,Rf_!M},\qquad\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id},M}=1,$$
with canonical composition coordinates understood. Evaluation-defined finite and integral Hom comparisons and unit/counit-preserving exceptional coefficient comparisons intertwine this entire chain term by term, so the composition equation is preserved by the stated coefficient changes. No exchange of Verdier duality with arbitrary pullback is asserted.

source.place: Agent-formulated sub-obligation for Verdier exchange: typed representing Hom chain on the preserved finite-Tor domain; returned proof steps 11,12

proof.text: Work first at finite or integral coefficients, on the full common finite-Tor domains of [lem-pod-hom-chain-ctf-domains], which places every object of the chain in $D^b_{ctf}$. Put $G_f=f^!$, $Q_f=Rf_*$, $A_f=Q_fH_X(M,G_fN)$ and $B_f=H_Y(F_fM,N)$. The counit-formula node supplies the natural bijection $\Phi^N_T:\operatorname{Hom}(T,A_f)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,B_f)$, with precisely the five transpositions in the question in reverse order: its projection arrow is precomposition with $\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,T}$. Consequently its inverse is the displayed chain, with precomposition by $\operatorname{PF}^{-1}$. All these bijections use the specified ordinary and exceptional adjunctions; no ambient exceptional adjoint or extra site-perfectness is needed. The same node states that $\Phi^N_T(u)=b_f\circ u$, where $b_f=\operatorname{curry}(p_N)$ and $p_N$ is its explicit counit/evaluation/projection composite. Thus this is the canonical tensor-Hom exchange, in the direction of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction].

source.place: Tensor-Hom chain underlying the sentence taking adjoint mates

proof.text: For completeness the representation of the inverse does not require tests outside the stated domain. Define $a_f=(\Phi^N_{B_f})^{-1}(1_{B_f})$. Then $b_fa_f=1_{B_f}$. Naturality gives $\Phi^N_{A_f}(a_fb_f)=b_fa_fb_f=b_f=\Phi^N_{A_f}(1_{A_f})$, so injectivity gives $a_fb_f=1_{A_f}$. Naturality of the inverse now gives $(\Phi^N_T)^{-1}(v)=a_fv$. Here $A_f$ and $B_f$ are allowed tests: [lem-pod-hom-chain-ctf-domains] states that $A_N,B_N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, and that $Rf^!N$, $L_N$, $Lf^*T$ and $M\otimes^LLf^*T$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, on which all five bijections are defined. This proves the assertion of the statement that all representing objects and tests lie in the common constructible finite-Tor categories. Equality of such represented maps can therefore be checked on every input arrow and finally on the identity test. Stage-3 Lean proof: apply the supplied test naturality of Phi to the identity and to a_f. Its inverse law gives Phi(a_f)=1_B; injectivity gives both inverse identities and Phi^{-1}(v)=v;a_f. Applying Phi to both sides and using its second-variable naturality also proves the representing-map naturality square. These arguments are implemented in representing_chain and chain_naturality, without new obligations.

Let $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$; then $G_gN\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ by [lem-pod-hom-chain-ctf-domains] for $g$, so the chain for $f$ applies with $G_gN$ in place of $N$. Let $v:T\to Q_gQ_fH_X(M,G_fG_gN)$. Under the ordinary adjunction for the composite, followed by uncurrying, let its image be $b:M\otimes P_fP_gT\to G_fG_gN$. The pasted ordinary counit in [fix-prop-adjunctions](3) identifies this with successive ordinary transposition. Apply $\Phi_f^{G_gN}$ inside $Q_g$, then $\Phi_g^N$. By the counit formula and naturality, the resulting arrow $T\to H_Z(F_gF_fM,N)$ uncurries to
$$\epsilon_g\circ F_g(\epsilon_f)\circ F_gF_f(b)\circ F_g(\operatorname{PF}_{f,M,P_gT})\circ\operatorname{PF}_{g,F_fM,T}.$$
The component of $\epsilon_f$ is at $G_gN$, and that of $\epsilon_g$ is at $N$. This follows simply by substituting the formula $\epsilon_hF_h(-)$ for exceptional inverse transposition twice. The ordinary transpositions and the tensor reassociations are inserted in their canonical coordinates.

source.place: Pasting the two tensor-Hom chains: explicit inverse-chain formula

proof.text: Use lem-sf-verdier-ordinary-tensor-transport for the inverse ordinary and tensor transposes. Apply lem-sf-verdier-projection-exceptional-paste to the resulting b. Test naturality of counit_formula identifies the f inverse chain inside g direct image. The shared Y tensor inverse cancels its transpose. This gives reverse_chain_paste. Invert the two Hom bijections and cancel the direct image of the f exchange isomorphism to prove ChainComposition on every input arrow. The final cancellation uses a generic proved functor-image isomorphism cancellation lemma; Verdier specialization uses a generic proved naturality paste with the identity test and second-variable naturality.

source.place: Projection diamonds and associativity; taking adjoint mates gives the corresponding equations for Verdier exchange.

proof.text:
Write $x=gf$, $\alpha:F_gF_f\cong F_x$, and $c:G_fG_g\cong G_x$ for the canonical conjugate. In the same coordinates, the one-map chain for $x$ uncurries to $\epsilon_xF_x(cb)\operatorname{PF}_x$. The exceptional-compositor equation says
$$\epsilon_xF_x(c)\alpha_{G_fG_gN}=\epsilon_gF_g(\epsilon_f).$$
The projection associativity pentagon says that $\operatorname{PF}_x$, transported through $\alpha$ and $P_x\cong P_fP_g$, is $F_g(\operatorname{PF}_f)\operatorname{PF}_g$. Substitute these two equalities in the one-map expression and use naturality of $\alpha$ with $b$. The result is exactly the expression in step 3. Injectivity of uncurrying and ordinary transposition gives equality on the original $v$. Inverting these equal bijections proves equality of the forward Hom chains, not merely existence of two isomorphisms. The projection/exceptional calculation is isolated as lem-sf-verdier-projection-exceptional-paste, strictly a part of the chain, while the ordinary/tensor calculation is proved separately.

source.place: Projection pentagon and pasted exceptional counit

proof.text: Take $N=\omega_Z$. The exceptional mate cocycles, applied to $f,g,a_Z$, identify the single structure comparison $G_x\omega_Z\cong\omega_X$ with $G_fG_g\omega_Z\to G_f\omega_Y\to\omega_X$. Thus the equality of step 4, after this substitution, is the composition equation for the Verdier arrows as defined in [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data]; [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] identifies these arrows with its canonical isomorphisms. Apply the identity test from step 2 to get the stated equality of morphisms. For the identity map use [lem-sf-verdier-identity-projection] only for the normalized pullback unit and its tensor projection triangle. For any reverse-chain input z, ordinary inverse transposition becomes p_T;z;r, exceptional inverse transposition becomes q;b;e, and source naturality of tensor transposition moves p_T outside. Substitute the projection triangle. Evaluation naturality in the first Hom input and inverse braiding naturality identify the final tensor transpose with postcomposition by H(q_M,1). The two tensor transposes cancel. Apply this identity to the forward representative, whose reverse transpose is identity, then cancel H(q_M,1) by its inverse. Naturality of r identifies the resulting arrow with epsilon followed by identityDirect. All of these adjunction and tensor calculations are proved in Lean; only the tensor projection triangle is split off. For stage_specialization, use projection naturality in its test object. In Lean, expand the inverse tensor-Hom map as tensor(v,1) followed by evaluation, move v across projection with this law, and use source naturality of the exceptional, tensor-Hom and ordinary adjunctions. At identity the chain is inverseComponent by the tensor-Hom counit law. Conclusion.components identifies the published exchange, and target naturality moves the dualizing comparison past the last two transposes.

source.place: Taking adjoint mates gives the Verdier composition and unit equations

proof.text: For the individual ordinary and exceptional coefficient transposes, apply the inverse Hom equivalence to each proposed equation. Expanding inverse transposition gives left-adjoint image followed by counit. The supplied counit comparison and naturality of the inverse left comparison give identical arrows; the Hom inverse law cancels the original transpose. The same argument applies to each tensor comparison, which need not be invertible on the Hom side. The projection equation is literally the field Comparison.projection. For the forward-chain square use the reverse-chain square of [lem-sf-tensor-hom-coefficient-transposes] at z=Phi^{-1}(v); injectivity of the changed Phi gives the desired forward equation. This proves coefficient_transposes. For composition_after_change, apply TZ to the original ChainComposition equation, postcompose with the inverse source coordinate, substitute that forward coefficient square, and postcompose with the changed source coordinate. Functoriality and the coordinate inverse identity cancel the inserted pair. These statements are implemented in Lean with no new obligations; the coefficient dependency retains the underlying finite/integral evaluation and unit/counit calculations.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons: evaluation, adjunctions and projection, term by term

proof.text: Finally use the rational and common-stage clause of [lem-sf-tensor-hom-coefficient-transposes]. It sends the integral $\Gamma$ bijections, their representing inverse maps, and their composition equations to the localized Hom groups. The exceptional rational comparisons preserve evaluations, units and counits by [lem-coef-rational-operations], while the mate cocycles identify the rationalized structure comparisons. At algebraically closed coefficients choose one common finite coefficient field for the finitely many inputs, arrows and equalities in the calculation; the same clause makes the result independent of enlargement and of representatives. This proves the Hom-chain, Verdier and coefficient assertions at the two field stages as well. This passage uses actual localization and common-stage maps, not reduction of a field object to a finite quotient.
